title: Automated triage and rollback runbook for embedding + reranker config changes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an automated triage and rollback runbook that ties offline embedding+reranker eval signals (recall/precision deltas, cohort drift, synthetic probe failures) to safe, auditable rollback and human-in-the-loop escalation paths. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect and time-to-mitigate regressions caused by config flips or model swaps while keeping noise low for production customers.
background: We see periodic precision/regression blips after config changes (batching, KV cache policy, quantization profiles) and occasional reranker recall degradation after model swaps. Current reaction is ad-hoc: on-call manually inspects dashboards and owns rollback. This ticket creates a deterministic, automated safety net with clear triage steps and automation hooks for staged rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A webhook/CI hook that receives a config change event and triggers pre-change snapshot and automated offline eval run within 15 minutes
A2: Eval harness computes cohorted recall@k and precision@k, plus drift score; any regression beyond configured thresholds triggers a triage workflow

A3: Triage workflow classifies regression severity (false-positive, config-related, model-quality) using signal ensemble and routes to on-call or auto-rollback depending on severity and customer impact

A4: Safe rollback automation that performs canary revert to previous model/config with automated smoke checks and an audit trail (links to PR and runbook) in under 10 minutes when auto-rollback is allowed
A5: Dashboards and alerting (Grafana + PagerDuty stub) that show pre/post change deltas, synthetic probe traces, and the decision path for each rollback
A6: Documentation (runbook + postmortem template) and at least one simulated drill completed with SRE/ML owners
tasks: T1: Implement change-event listener and payload schema (change fingerprint, author, PR link, change type)
T2: Wire up offline eval job template that runs on a shadow sample and golden synthetic probes
T3: Build a signal scoring service that ingests eval metrics and outputs a severity score and recommended action
T4: Implement rollback orchestrator that can revert model/config in staging and production canaries with safety gates
T5: Create dashboard panels for pre/post deltas, cohort breakdown, and change history
T6: Author runbook and escalation playbook; run tabletop exercise
rollback_playbook: Step 1: On change-event receive pre-change baseline snapshot (embeddings + reranker inference traces)
Step 2: Launch offline evals on last-24h production sample plus golden probes
Step 3: Compute ensemble severity score; if score >= auto-rollback threshold and customer_impact != high then trigger automated canary rollback
Step 4: After rollback, run smoke tests (latency, success rate, 10 synthetic probes). If smoke passes, promote revert and notify stakeholders
Step 5: If score is elevated but below auto-rollback, create a triage ticket, attach eval artifacts and recommended remediation, and page ML on-call
Step 6: Record decision and artifacts to audit log and tag change PR with 'regression-investigated' label
test_plan: Simulated change: flip quantization profile in staging and verify eval harness detects expected metric shifts
Introduce synthetic regressions in reranker (downgrade model weights) and verify auto-rollback triggers in allowed scenarios
False-positive resilience test: noisy traffic scenario to validate triage scoring reduces noisy rollbacks
Drill: run a tabletop exercise with SRE, ML, PM and document timing and gaps
notes: Decision: start with a conservative auto-rollback threshold (0.08 recall@10 absolute drop or 15% relative) to minimize false positives
Trade-off: automatic rollback lowers MTTR but could mask intermittent upstream issues; mitigation will be a post-rollback golden evaluation and manual approval window for high-impact customers
We will fingerprint changes by (model-version, quantization-profile, batching-policy, KV-cache-setting) to group incidents and speed root-cause
